chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, the heart trembles between the chest and the throat until it is tied to faith; so when it is tied to faith, it settles, and that is the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And whoever believes in Allah, He guides his heart.'

key_terms.الْقَلْبُ: The heart (spiritual/intellectual center, not just physical)

ai.seo_question: What happens to the heart before and after firm faith is established?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith elucidates the physiological-spiritual manifestation of Iman, where the heart's initial tremor (tarajjud) signifies the struggle of faith before settling into tranquility (qarr). Scholars interpret this as a sign of the believer's sincerity, linking the physical sensation to the divine promise of guidance found in Surah At-Taghabun. This narrative underscores the Shia emphasis on the heart as a living organ that responds dynamically to spiritual truth.
